## Summary

Implemented `syncbox sync <dir> --server <url>` for ticket 10:

- **`client/src/sync.js`** — walks `<dir>` and lists server blobs in parallel, then for each key present on only one side transfers it to the other (push-like/pull-like, no deletions). For keys present on both sides with differing SHA-256, it consults a local manifest recording the SHA-256 both sides last agreed on: if only one side moved away from that baseline, that side wins unconditionally; if both did (or there's no baseline yet), it's a real conflict resolved by the spec's fixed rule — newer `modified_at`/mtime wins, local wins on a tie.
- **`client/src/manifest.js`** — reads/writes the last-known-common-state manifest at `<dir>/.syncbox/manifest.json`, the mechanism for tracking baseline state across separate `sync` invocations (each `run-client` call is a throwaway container, so this has to live inside the mounted `<dir>` to persist).
- **`client/src/walk.js`** — excludes the reserved `.syncbox` directory from the recursive file walk, so `sync`'s own bookkeeping is never itself treated as a syncable file (also affects `push`/`status`, harmlessly).
- **`client/src/cli.js`** — wired up the `sync` command (was previously falling through to "not implemented yet"); removed the now-dead fallback block.
- **`client/test/sync.test.js`** — new test suite covering all six required scenarios (local-only→upload, server-only→download, local-only-changed, server-only-changed, conflict-newer-wins in both directions, conflict-tie→local-wins), plus no-op-when-matching, nested keys, manifest exclusion across two runs, directory auto-creation, and unreachable-server handling. Conflict tests deliberately set local mtime *older* than the server's real timestamp for the "changed-only-on-one-side" cases, to prove resolution is baseline-driven rather than an accidental mtime race.

No changes were needed to `run-client`, `docker-compose.yml`, or the client `Dockerfile` — they already generically forward `sync` and copy all of `src/`.

**One important caveat:** this sandbox has no working POSIX shell (`Bash` and `Monitor` both fail with "No suitable shell found," confirmed both directly and via a sub-agent), so I was unable to actually run `./run-tests` or exercise `run-client sync` through Docker to confirm everything passes end-to-end. I reviewed the logic and test setup carefully by hand and traced through each scenario, but please run `./run-tests` yourself to confirm before considering this done — I couldn't complete that verification step.
